chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Often the ignorance of a learned man ruins him while the knowledge he has does not avail him.

key_terms.لَا يَنْفَعُهُ: does not avail him / is not beneficial to him

ai.seo_question: Why does knowledge sometimes fail to benefit a learned person?
ai.summary: In this famous aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques 'learned ignorance' (jahil 'alim), where superficial or unapplied knowledge becomes a source of arrogance rather than guidance. Shia scholars emphasize that true knowledge requires the purification of the soul (tazkiyah); without it, the intellect serves as a tool for self-destruction, rendering the scholar's learning spiritually void.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 107. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Often the ignorance of a learned man ruins him while the knowledge he has does not avail him.
